Sometimes a jammed flywheel can be freed safely; other times a cracked housing or burned-out motor means replacement makes more sense. Call us to review your kitchen sink setup.

symptoms.title: Disposal hums but blades do not spin
symptoms.text: A jammed flywheel from a bone, fruit pit, or silverware keeps the motor locked and quickly trips the overload button.

symptoms.title: Water dripping from the bottom housing
symptoms.text: Leaks coming through the bottom casing or reset button usually mean internal motor seals have failed.

symptoms.title: No sound at all when switched on
symptoms.text: A tripped red reset button, dead wall switch, or burned-out motor windings can stop the unit completely.

symptoms.title: Leaking at the sink flange or drain elbow
symptoms.text: Dried plumber's putty, loose mounting rings, or cracked dishwasher discharge hoses drip whenever the sink drains.

symptoms.title: Slow kitchen sink drainage
symptoms.text: Fibrous food scraps like celery, potato peels, and pasta often pack into the P-trap or horizontal wall arm.

symptoms.title: Loud grinding or rattling noises
symptoms.text: Worn bearings or metal debris trapped inside the grind chamber create harsh vibration under the sink.

methods.title: Safe Jam Clearing & Trap Cleaning
methods.whenItFits: Locked flywheels, tripped overload switches, or clogged P-traps
methods.text: With power disconnected, we free stuck impellers using proper hex-wrench and tong tools, clear packed food waste from the trap arm, and test motor draw and drainage.

methods.title: Sink Flange & Discharge Seal Repair
methods.whenItFits: Leaks around the top sink mount, dishwasher nipple, or rubber drain gasket
methods.text: When the motor itself is dry and strong, resealing the sink basket flange or replacing cracked discharge gaskets stops cabinet water damage without replacing the entire unit.

methods.title: Quiet High-Torque Disposal Installation
methods.whenItFits: Leaking bottom housings, burned-out motors, or upgrading noisy builder-grade units
methods.text: We remove the failed unit, align the mounting collar cleanly, connect the dishwasher knockout and P-trap with proper slope, and verify leak-free operation.

phoenixAngle.heading: Kitchen Drain & Disposal Care in Phoenix Homes
paragraphs: In Phoenix homes, kitchen disposals share drain lines with dishwashers and hard-water mineral film. Grinding fibrous peels or pouring cooking grease down the sink lets fatty residue congeal along horizontal branch lines just beyond the P-trap, gradually slowing kitchen drainage and causing odors.

Running cold water while grinding small food scraps and flushing with plenty of water afterward helps move solids cleanly out toward the main drain. If your sink still backs up when the disposal runs, the clog likely sits further down the kitchen branch line and needs professional snaking.

facts.text: Hard water minerals combine with kitchen soaps and fats to form stubborn buildup in sink drain lines.

costFactors.intro: Garbage disposal service cost depends on whether the unit only needs jam clearing and resealing or full replacement with a new horsepower tier.

factors.title: Repair vs. new unit installation
factors.text: Clearing a jam or tightening a discharge elbow costs less than supplying and mounting a brand-new disposal.

factors.title: Horsepower and grind chamber material
factors.text: Standard 1/3-HP builder units differ in cost and longevity from quieter 3/4-HP or 1-HP stainless-steel models.

factors.title: Under-sink drain modifications
factors.text: Deep farmhouse sinks or new disposal heights sometimes require adjusting the P-trap and wall stub-out alignment.

factors.title: Hardwired vs. cord-and-plug setup
factors.text: Units wired directly into a junction box require different connection steps than standard plug-in outlets.

faqs.q: Why does my garbage disposal just hum when I flip the switch?
faqs.a: A humming sound means power is reaching the motor, but something is physically jamming the flywheel blades—often a small bone, fruit pit, or bottle cap. Turn the switch off immediately so the motor does not overheat, and call a plumber if the reset button keeps popping.

faqs.q: Can a leaking garbage disposal be repaired?
faqs.a: If water is dripping from the top sink flange, the rubber drain elbow, or the dishwasher hose connection, tightening or replacing the gasket usually fixes it. If water is dripping directly out of the bottom motor housing, the internal seal has failed and the unit must be replaced.

faqs.q: Is it safe to reach inside my garbage disposal to grab a dropped spoon?
faqs.a: No—never reach your hand inside a garbage disposal, even if the wall switch is off. Always turn off power at the breaker or unplug the unit underneath the sink, and use long tongs or pliers—or let a plumber retrieve it safely.

faqs.q: What size garbage disposal should I install in a family kitchen?
faqs.a: While 1/3-HP or 1/2-HP units handle light scraps, most busy Phoenix households prefer a 3/4-HP or 1-HP disposal with stainless steel grind components, which resists hard-water corrosion, jams less often, and runs noticeably quieter under daily kitchen sink and dishwasher use.

faqs.q: Why does my kitchen sink back up when I turn on the disposal?
faqs.a: A disposal pushes pulverized food and water into the drain quickly, which exposes partial grease or food clogs sitting in the P-trap or horizontal kitchen branch line. If clearing the trap does not help, the drain line itself needs snaking.

faqs.q: Will a new garbage disposal connect to my dishwasher?
faqs.a: Yes. New disposals include a side inlet port for the dishwasher drain hose. During installation, we knock out the factory plug, secure the hose with a proper clamp, and verify a high-loop routing to prevent sink water from backing into your dishwasher.
